Routes

HTTP routes, route modules and static asset serving.

This document lists the HTTP routes the service exposes and how route modules are organised.

Route table

Method Path Auth Handler Response
Method Path Auth Handler Response
— — — — —
GET / none home controller home/index view (Dashboard)
GET /about none about controller about/index view
GET /health none health controller JSON { "message": "success" }, 200
GET /cookies none cookies controller cookies/policy view
POST /cookies none cookies controller JSON or redirect, see cookie consent
GET /favicon.ico none serve-static-files.js 204 No Content (production and test only)
GET /public/{param*} none serve-static-files.js or Vite middleware Built client assets, see client assets

Route handlers and the /cookies routes are wired in router.js.

Route modules

Each feature lives in src/server/routes/<name>/:

  • index.js exports a Hapi plugin that calls server.route().
  • controller.js exports the handler (and any validation options).
  • index.njk is the view, when the route renders HTML. Views are referenced by path relative to src/server/routes, for example home/index.
  • controller.test.js holds the Vitest tests.

The home and about routes are example pages from the CDP template. The health route must stay: it is used by the platform.

Static assets

  • Outside production and test, router.js starts Vite in middleware mode and mounts it at /public through @defra/hapi-connect.
  • In production or test, serveStaticFiles serves ${assetPath}/{param*} from .public with a cache lifetime of staticCacheTimeout (default one week).
  • The /favicon.ico route is registered only in the production or test branch.

Request logging

The request logger ignores /public/*, /health, and /favicon.ico (see request-logger.js).
